Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old man with 4-day history of sore throat, rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, new dry cough, night sweats, myalgias, intermittent headache, and initial fever now settling.
- Impression of viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza; conservative management advised with red-flag review instructions.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Viral upper respiratory tract infection / possible early influenza.
  • Onset: 4 days ago after exposure to unwell colleague.  
  • Symptoms: sore throat (odynophagia first 2 days, now resolving), persistent nasal congestion with clear discharge, dry constant cough since yesterday, night sweats, fatigue, myalgias (past 2 days), intermittent generalized headaches, initial fever responsive to paracetamol/ibuprofen, mild exertional shortness of breath but no chest pain at rest.  
  • Pertinent negatives: no ear pain/discharge, no vision changes, no photophobia, no nausea/vomiting, bowels and urine normal, no rash.  
  • Examination: none recorded (telehealth).  
  • Clinical impression: self-limiting viral URTI; flu not excluded.

Issue 2:
- Lifestyle risk: Occasional cigar smoking and social alcohol use.
  • No current alcohol misuse; occasional cigars at work events.

Issue 3:
- Family history of chronic disease.
  • Grandmother with type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather with eczema.

Medications:
- Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) – for fever/pain relief.
- Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) – for fever/pain relief.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Denies chronic medical conditions; otherwise fit and well.

Social History:
- Lives alone; employed as an accountant.  
- Smoking: occasional cigars.  
- Alcohol: occasional social drinking.

Preventative History:
- No preventive screenings or vaccinations discussed/documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings provided (telehealth consultation).

Plan:
- Rest; consider 1–2 days off work.  
- Maintain adequate oral hydration.  
- Continue paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed for fever, pain.  
- Return earlier if high fever recurs, breathing becomes labored, or chest pain develops; otherwise follow up next week if no improvement.  
- Smoking: encourage avoidance of cigars; offer smoking cessation resources if desired.  
- Consider influenza vaccination when well (not discussed during call).

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: vitals, objective physical exam, complete medication reconciliation, vaccination status, allergy verification beyond drugs (e.g., food/latex).  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio with minimal filler; adequate clinical detail but limited objective data due to telehealth setting.
